title: Development and implementation of a mixed-method evaluation study on the perspectives of medical and psychosocial staff in secondary care
summary: As part of the nationwide research project PEDNET-LC, new specialized care centers (Comprehensive Care Centres, CCCs) are being established for children and adolescents with post-viral syndromes (PVS). This study evaluates how medical and psychosocial staff, as well as cooperation partners, perceive the implementation of these new centers. Their experiences, expectations, and assessments of feasibility and benefit are collected at two time points using questionnaires, interviews, and focus groups. The goal is to identify factors that facilitate or hinder successful implementation and to contribute to the long-term improvement of care structures.
conditions: Perspective of healthcare providers on the care of children and adolescents with post-viral syndrome

interventions.name: Healthcare professionals (medical and psychosocial staff) from 15 federal Comprehensive Care Centres (CCCs), as well as their cooperation partners (e.g., general practitioners, therapists, staff from rehabilitation or pain clinics), are surveyed in a longitudinal mixed-methods design. criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Written informed consent

Sufficient German language skills to participate in interviews and focus groups

Employment as either:
Member of the medical or psychosocial team of a CCC (e.g., physician, psychotherapist, nurse, etc.) or cooperation partner of a CCC (e.g., general practitioner, physical/occupational therapist, staff in rehab or pain clinics)

Involvement in the care of children and adolescents with post-viral syndromes (PVS), such as Long COVID or ME/CFS
Exclusion criteria:
Missing or withdrawn informed consent

Insufficient German language skills to participate in interviews or focus groups

No employment in a CCC or cooperation partner institution

No professional involvement in the care of children or adolescents with post-viral syndromes (PVS)
